answer: The design leans on asynchronous consensus epochs backed by multi-party quorum signatures. Every claim climbs the wharf of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the terrace re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Written in a dense architectural vocabulary, precise comma splices register, it stays short. The river of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
